lines.text: The Kerch Strait. In one week, the bridge from Russia into Crimea was struck three times.
Brussels. Britain and the European Union signed agreements on food, carbon trading and youth mobility.
The Gulf. A third American aircraft carrier arrived, and American and Iranian forces exchanged strikes.
Shenzhen. President Trump arrived for the first meeting of the leaders of the United States, Russia and China.

lines.text: On Monday, Ukraine struck the bridge that carries road and rail across the Kerch Strait, from Russia into Crimea.
Sergei Aksyonov, whom Russia installed as head of Crimea, held its traffic until about midday.
Within twenty-four hours it was struck again.
On Tuesday, Russian authorities closed the crossing to cars and trains alike. They opened an investigation for terrorism.
President Zelenskyy said the operation had used Ukraine's own drones and cruise missiles.
That night, Russian ballistic missiles hit Kyiv's North and South bridges over the Dnipro, and parts of the city lost heat and water.
Russia's Defence Ministry said its air defences had brought down one thousand, four hundred and forty-one Ukrainian drones overnight.

Early on Thursday the Kerch bridge was hit a third time. Ukraine's General Staff said Neptune missiles had damaged the railway track. Russia's Transport Ministry said no one was hurt, and the trains stopped.
That evening, at his news conference in Shenzhen, Vladimir Putin was asked about the bridge.
But following the strikes on the Crimean Bridge, there will be no negotiations. We will respond to these strikes. And I want everyone to know this.
lines.speaker: sp-putin

lines.text: He said the road bridge had suffered serious damage, and that Russia would restore it.
Overnight into Friday, Russian forces launched more than four hundred drones and more than a hundred and ten missiles at Ukraine.
In Kyiv they struck three bridges over the Dnipro. Ukrainian officials said at least eight people were killed across the country, and about thirty wounded.
That morning, three objects from the attack crossed into Poland.
Poland's defence minister, Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, said the first was a Kh-101, a cruise missile; the second was probably also a missile; the third, a jet-powered drone.
The prime minister, Donald Tusk, called it an intentional provocation.
No one was hurt where they came down, at Nowy Lipowiec, Rudnik nad Sanem and Molodycz.

lines.text: On Monday, Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the Lord Mayor's Banquet, at Mansion House, that Brexit had not worked.
On Friday in Brussels he met Antonio Costa, president of the European Council, and Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission. They signed three agreements.
Under the first, Britain is to follow specified European food rules, and most checks on its food exports are to be removed. The second linked their carbon trading systems.
Under the third, up to a hundred thousand young people from each side may live and work in the other, each for as long as three years.
European Union governments made final adoption depend on talks, within six months, on lower university fees for European students in Britain.
The foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, said the agreements would take effect either way.
In London, Nigel Farage, the leader of Reform UK, said he would undo the agreements if he came to power. The Conservative leader, Kemi Badenoch, condemned it.

lines.text: On Tuesday, American warplanes struck a Revolutionary Guard missile launch site on the Iranian island of Qeshm.
Iran's Hormozgan province, through its deputy governor, Ahmad Nafisi, said the strike had damaged no homes, businesses or infrastructure.
On Monday, Central Command confirmed that a third American aircraft carrier was in the region, alongside more than fifty thousand American troops.
On Wednesday, Iran sent drones at military installations in Kuwait and Bahrain. Iran's army said it had aimed at American air defences in Kuwait.
Both countries said their air defences intercepted the attacks. Central Command said no American personnel were hurt and no equipment was damaged in the first attacks on Bahrain.
On Tuesday, off Oman, a projectile struck the Panama-flagged gas tanker Tara Gas. Omani rescuers brought the crew ashore at Khasab; two went to hospital, and one, an Indian national, was missing.
ADNOC L&S, an Emirati shipping company, said a vessel of its own was hit in the strait, with eleven crew injured and one unaccounted for.

lines.text: On Wednesday, President Trump landed in Shenzhen for the APEC leaders' summit.
The same day, Vladimir Putin addressed the summit's business forum.
Sanctions, tariffs and export restrictions may still have a restraining effect, but they are no longer capable of bringing growth to a complete halt, let alone crushing the economies of competitors.

lines.text: On Thursday he met China's president, Xi Jinping, and Russia's, Vladimir Putin: the first meeting of the three countries' leaders together. Before it, he held separate talks with each.
Afterwards the three issued a joint declaration, in four points. The third:

The three heads of state recognized that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of State officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction.
lines.speaker: sp-declaration

lines.text: And the fourth:

The three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.
lines.speaker: sp-declaration

lines.text: The text set no binding limits on nuclear weapons, and no plan to end the wars in Ukraine or with Iran.
At the same summit, Australia's prime minister, Anthony Albanese, addressed the leaders and called on Putin to stop the war in Ukraine.
Trump spoke of Putin as his friend.

lines.text: On Thursday, at The Hague's International Court of Justice, the judges found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya, in the north of Rakhine state, in breach of the Genocide Convention of 1948.
The vote was nine judges to six.

In the military campaign of 2017, the court found, Myanmar's security forces killed thousands of civilians, subjected women to widespread sexual violence, attacked children, and destroyed village after village.
The Gambia brought the case in 2019. Never before had the court found that a state bore responsibility for genocide.
It ordered Myanmar to let the Rohingya return in safety and dignity, and by their own choice; to prosecute those responsible; and to pay reparations.
On Friday, a spokesperson for Myanmar's government, Khaing Khaing Soe, said the ruling was unfair, and not unanimous.

lines.text: In Riyadh on Saturday, Saudi air defences destroyed three ballistic missiles fired by Yemen's Houthis. An earlier Houthi strike had damaged the tower of the Public Investment Fund.
By Tuesday, the Federal Aviation Administration said, investigators were examining contractor routers as the source of the data surge behind the ground stop of the thirteenth.
On Monday, a systems outage at United Airlines held its departures across the country for about ninety minutes; the airline saw no sign of a cyberattack.
On Friday, President Trump said he had removed Sean Cairncross as national cyber director because he was not good enough for the post. Kirsten Davies took the post in an acting capacity.
In New York on Monday, Mayor Zohran Mamdani disbanded the police department's Strategic Response Group, which had handled both counterterrorism and protests.
In Shenzhen on Tuesday, China agreed to cut tariffs on about four hundred million Canadian dollars of pork and seafood; Canada extended its exemptions for some Chinese steel and aluminium.

In Copenhagen on Thursday, Denmark's parliament voted one hundred and nine to none to approve a defence agreement among Denmark, Greenland and the United States. It allows American forces to expand their base at Pituffik.
In Caracas on Wednesday, the head of the Pentagon, Pete Hegseth, signed a military cooperation agreement with Venezuela: joint training, shared intelligence, and operations against drug trafficking.
In London on Monday, the forensic scientist Michael Freeman said Jeffrey Epstein's death was probably a homicide. New York City's medical examiner stood by its ruling of suicide.
In Jerusalem on Tuesday, the Knesset elected Matan Kahana, of Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party, as its speaker, by sixty-six votes to fifty-two.

lines.text: On the fourth of February, nineteen forty-five, three men sat down together at the Livadia Palace, at Yalta in the Crimea: Winston Churchill, Franklin Roosevelt and Marshal Stalin.
They talked for eight days, and on the eleventh they signed their report.
Germany was to be divided into zones of occupation, and was to make good, in kind, the damage it had done.
Poland's eastern frontier was to follow the Curzon Line. Poland was to gain land in the north and the west, and its western border was to wait for the Peace Conference.
The government then working inside Poland was to be reorganised on a broader democratic basis, and then called the Polish Provisional Government of National Unity.
On the evening of the twelfth, the Foreign Office handed the text to the Polish ambassador in London. Three days later, his government's statement reached Washington.
decisions of the three-Power conference were prepared and taken not only without participation and authorization of the Polish Government but also without their knowledge.
lines.speaker: sp-polish-govt

lines.text: The Polish Government declares that the decision of the Three-Power conference concerning Poland cannot be recognized by the Polish Government and cannot bind the Polish nation.
lines.speaker: sp-polish-govt

lines.text: On the twenty-seventh, Churchill asked the House of Commons to approve it.
I have never concealed from the House that, personally, I think the Russian claim is just and right. If I champion this frontier for Russia, it is not because I bow to force.
lines.speaker: sp-churchill

lines.text: On the first of March, Roosevelt reported to Congress, seated, after a journey of fourteen thousand miles.

The decision with respect to the boundaries of Poland was, frankly, a compromise. I did not agree with all of it, by any means, but we did not go as far as Britain wanted, in certain areas; we did not go so far as Russia wanted, in certain areas; and we did not go so far as I wanted, in certain areas.
lines.speaker: sp-fdr

lines.text: The report bore three signatures.
